name: How do fourplex projects handle demolition and lot clearing?

mainEntity.name: What should owners expect when an existing house must be demolished for a fourplex build?
mainEntity.text: What should owners expect when an existing house must be demolished for a fourplex build?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many fourplex projects start with an existing single-family house or older structure that has to come down first. Searchers need to know that demolition is not just a quick teardown. It can require utility coordination, asbestos or hazardous-material review, temporary site protection, and debris disposal planning. If the lot is tight, the demolition plan also needs to protect neighboring structures and preserve access for excavation and construction. A strong page should explain that clearing the site early and correctly can prevent downstream delays. That practical guidance is more useful than simply saying demolition is part of the project.
acceptedAnswer.description: Demolition can add permitting, utility disconnects, hauling, environmental checks, and timing coordination before vertical construction begins. On Los Angeles infill sites, clearing the lot is often a separate project phase with its own risks and costs.
